assumptions: The period-3 measurements are representative of busy periods under the same seeds and demand.
The companies' votes reflect their measured utilities and would not change without a remedy.
The road violation counts in the table are comparable across proposals.
Waiting one more period does not cause lasting harm to customers beyond the measured gap.
unknowns: The per-company, per-type and per-severity breakdown of the added road violations under block_k=2, and whether the Major eviction sanctions fall mostly on C.
The combined effect of block_k=2 with an intermediate lambda (for example 0.25) or with sanctions redistributed away from C.
Whether B or C would vote for block_k=2 with a targeted remedy, and their stated reasons.
Next period's demand level, and whether option 2's gain (3/5 seeds this period) is robust.
Whether the companies' behaviour would drift over time if sanctions were removed.
